cast.name: God (Yahweh)
aliases: the Judge of all the earth
cast.note: The creator God of Genesis and the God of Israel who speaks and acts across the Hebrew Bible and Acts; the same divine presence under each title and every book.

cast.name: Abram / Abraham the patriarch
cast.note: Son of Terah, called from Haran and renamed Abraham; the patriarch of Genesis, mentioned as father in the Gospels and Acts.

cast.name: Simeon son of Jacob
cast.note: Son of Jacob and Leah, involved in the Shechem massacre and held by Joseph in Egypt.

cast.name: Simeon the righteous man
cast.note: Devout man in Jerusalem who blesses the infant Jesus in the temple; distinct from the patriarch Simeon.

cast.name: Levi son of Jacob
cast.note: Son of Jacob and Leah, who with Simeon avenges Dinah; a patriarch of Genesis, not a tax collector.

cast.name: Matthew / Levi the tax collector
cast.note: Tax collector called to follow Jesus, named Matthew in Matthew and Levi in Luke; also the apostle Matthew in the apostle lists.

cast.name: Gad son of Jacob
cast.note: Son of Jacob and Zilpah, a patriarch named in Genesis.

cast.name: Gad the prophet
cast.note: Prophet who advises David to leave the stronghold; not a son of Jacob.

cast.name: Joseph son of Jacob
cast.note: Son of Jacob and Rachel, sold into Egypt and later vizier to Pharaoh; Genesis figure, also recounted by Stephen.

cast.name: Joseph husband of Mary
cast.note: Carpenter of Nazareth, husband of Mary and foster father of Jesus, of David's house.

cast.name: Joseph of Arimathaea
aliases: Joseph, a member of the council
cast.note: Council member who asks Pilate for Jesus' body and buries him; distinct from the husband of Mary.

cast.name: Moses
cast.note: Hebrew leader who leads Israel out of Egypt and receives the law; appears in the Gospels and Acts as the lawgiver.

cast.name: Pharaoh of the Exodus
cast.note: The Egyptian king who enslaves Israel and resists the plagues, also referenced by Stephen.

cast.name: Miriam
cast.note: Sister of Moses and Aaron and prophetess who leads the song after the sea crossing; likely the same as the sister who watches the basket.

cast.name: Amalekites
cast.note: People who attack Israel at Rephidim and later raid Ziklag; the same nation in both books.

cast.name: Samuel
cast.note: Prophet and judge who anoints Saul and David, son of Hannah.

cast.name: Hophni
cast.note: Wicked son of Eli, priest at Shiloh, killed at Aphek.

cast.name: Phinehas son of Eli
cast.note: Wicked son of Eli, killed with Hophni at Aphek; not the later Phinehas son of Eleazar.

cast.name: Saul the king
cast.note: First king of Israel, son of Kish, rejected by Samuel and dying on Gilboa.

cast.name: Saul of Tarsus / Paul
cast.note: Pharisee persecutor converted on the road to Damascus, later the apostle Paul; the main figure of Acts from chapter 7 on.

cast.name: Jonathan son of Saul
cast.note: Eldest son of Saul and close friend of David, who dies on Gilboa.

cast.name: Ishvi son of Saul
cast.note: Son of Saul named in a genealogy, killed on Gilboa with Jonathan.

cast.name: Malchishua son of Saul
cast.note: Son of Saul killed on Gilboa with Jonathan.

cast.name: David king of Israel
cast.note: Youngest son of Jesse, anointed by Samuel, slayer of Goliath and king of Israel; appears as king in the Gospels and Acts.

cast.name: Abinadab son of Jesse
cast.note: Brother of David who passed before Samuel; not the Abinadab who hosted the ark.

cast.name: Shammah son of Jesse
cast.note: Brother of David who passed before Samuel and fought with Saul.

cast.name: Joel son of Samuel
cast.note: Eldest son of Samuel, a corrupt judge at Beersheba.

cast.name: Abijah son of Samuel
cast.note: Second son of Samuel, a corrupt judge at Beersheba.

cast.name: Israelite army and people
cast.note: The Israelite army and assembly in 1 Samuel acting collectively.

cast.name: Jerusalem temple crowd
aliases: The Jews from Asia and the temple crowd
cast.note: Jews from Asia and the crowd who seize Paul in the temple in Acts 21.

cast.name: Jesus of Nazareth
cast.note: Central figure of the Gospels and Acts, the crucified and risen Christ; the same figure across Matthew, Luke, John and Acts.

cast.name: Blind man of Jericho
cast.note: Unnamed blind beggar near Jericho who receives sight in Luke 18; distinct from Bartimaeus.

cast.name: Mary mother of Jesus
cast.note: Mother of Jesus, betrothed to Joseph, present at Cana, the cross and the upper room.

cast.name: Mary Magdalene
aliases: Mary from whom seven demons had gone out
cast.note: Woman healed of seven demons who witnesses the crucifixion and the empty tomb.

cast.name: Mary of Bethany
aliases: the sister who sat at Jesus' feet
the woman who anointed the Lord
cast.note: Sister of Martha and Lazarus who sits at Jesus' feet and anoints him; not the mother of Jesus.

cast.name: Mary the mother of James
cast.note: Woman who goes to the tomb and tells the apostles, distinct from Mary the mother of Jesus in Luke's text.

cast.name: Mary mother of John Mark
aliases: Mary the mother of John Mark
cast.note: Woman in Jerusalem whose house hosts the praying believers in Acts 12.

cast.name: Herod the Great
aliases: the king of Judea in the days of Zacharias
cast.note: King of Judea who seeks the child Jesus and orders the killing of boys in Bethlehem.

cast.name: Herod Antipas the tetrarch
cast.note: Tetrarch of Galilee who executes John the Baptizer and mocks Jesus; son of Herod the Great.

cast.name: Herod Agrippa I
cast.note: King who kills James and imprisons Peter in Acts 12, struck dead by an angel; distinct from Herod Antipas.

cast.name: John the Baptizer
aliases: the voice crying in the wilderness
cast.note: Preacher in the wilderness who baptizes Jesus and is imprisoned and beheaded by Herod Antipas.

cast.name: John the apostle son of Zebedee
cast.note: Apostle and brother of James, one of the inner three disciples and companion of Peter in Acts.

cast.name: Pharisees
cast.note: Religious leaders who repeatedly oppose or question Jesus across the Gospels.

cast.name: Sadducees
cast.note: Religious party who deny the resurrection and question Jesus about it.

cast.name: Scribes / teachers of the law
cast.note: Teachers of the law who debate Jesus and join the chief priests against him.

cast.name: The lawyer who tests Jesus
cast.note: Single scribe who asks Jesus which commandment is greatest; a member of the scribes.

cast.name: Satan (the devil)
cast.note: The adversary who tempts Jesus in the wilderness and is called the prince of demons; the same figure in Matthew and Luke.

cast.name: Simon Peter
cast.note: Fisherman from Galilee, first called disciple and apostle, renamed Cephas, who denies Jesus; the same individual across all four Gospels and Acts.

cast.name: Simon the Pharisee
cast.note: Pharisee host who rebukes the sinful woman at dinner; not the fisherman.

cast.name: Simon Magus
cast.note: Samaritan sorcerer who offers money for the Spirit; not Peter.

cast.name: Simon the tanner
cast.note: Tanner in Joppa whose house Peter lodges in; distinct from Peter and Simon Magus.

cast.name: Andrew
cast.note: Fisherman from Bethsaida, brother of Simon Peter, one of the first disciples and the twelve; the same individual in the Gospels, and a name-only apostle in Acts.

cast.name: James son of Zebedee
cast.note: Fisherman apostle, brother of John, present at the transfiguration and Gethsemane; the same individual in the Gospels and in Acts 12.

cast.name: James the brother of Jesus
cast.note: Leader of the Jerusalem assembly in Acts 15 and 21; distinct from James son of Zebedee.

cast.name: Judas Iscariot
aliases: one of the twelve who would betray him
cast.note: The apostle who keeps the money box and betrays Jesus; the same individual across the Gospels and Acts 1.

cast.name: Judas (not Iscariot)
cast.note: Disciple who asks at the supper why Jesus will reveal himself only to the disciples; distinct from the betrayer.

cast.name: Philip the apostle
cast.note: One of the twelve from Bethsaida who brings Nathanael and the Greeks to Jesus; the same apostle in Matthew, Luke, John and the Acts upper room list.

cast.name: Philip the evangelist
cast.note: One of the seven who preaches in Samaria and baptizes the Ethiopian eunuch; distinct from the apostle.

cast.name: Thomas
cast.note: Apostle called Didymus who doubts the resurrection until he sees Jesus; the fourth disciple named in John 21:2 is the same person.

cast.name: Bartholomew
cast.note: Apostle named only in the twelve-apostle lists; the same individual in each list.

cast.name: James son of Alphaeus
cast.note: Apostle named only in the twelve-apostle lists; distinct from James son of Zebedee.

cast.name: Simon the Zealot
aliases: Simon who was called the Zealot
cast.note: Apostle named only in the twelve-apostle lists; distinct from Simon Peter.

cast.name: Caiaphas
cast.note: High priest who plots Jesus' death and presides at his trial; the same individual in Matthew, John and Acts 4.

cast.name: Pontius Pilate
cast.note: Roman governor of Judea who tries Jesus and orders his crucifixion; the same individual across the Gospels and Acts.

cast.name: Barabbas
cast.note: Prisoner or robber released in place of Jesus; the same individual in all three Gospels.

cast.name: Roman soldiers
cast.note: Roman soldiers who mock, flog and crucify Jesus and guard the tomb, in the Gospels; the guards at the tomb are the same soldiers.

cast.name: Herod's soldiers
cast.note: Soldiers guarding Peter in prison in Acts 12; a separate body from the Gospel soldiers.

cast.name: Centurion of Capernaum
cast.note: Roman officer whose servant Jesus heals at a distance; in Matthew 8 and Luke 7 this is one individual.

cast.name: Centurion at the cross
cast.note: Officer who watches the crucifixion and declares Jesus the Son of God; a separate officer in each Gospel, identified as the same as the Capernaum centurion only by Matthew's link.

cast.name: Joseph of Arimathea
cast.note: Rich or secret disciple who buries Jesus in his new tomb; the same individual in Matthew and John.

cast.name: Simon of Cyrene
cast.note: Man compelled to carry Jesus' cross; distinct from Simon Peter.

cast.name: The leper
cast.note: Man healed of leprosy by Jesus; the same healing story in Matthew 8 and Luke 5.

cast.name: The paralytic
cast.note: Paralyzed man carried to Jesus, forgiven and healed; the same healing story in Matthew 9 and Luke 5.

cast.name: The disciples
cast.note: Jesus' followers as a body in Matthew and John.

cast.name: Caesar Augustus
cast.note: Roman emperor whose census decree opens Luke's birth narrative; a different Caesar appears in Acts.

cast.name: Caesar (emperor in Acts)
cast.note: Unnamed Roman emperor to whom Paul appeals in Acts 25; not Augustus of Luke 2.

cast.name: Judas son of James
cast.note: Apostle named in the twelve lists and Acts 1; the same individual in both.

cast.name: Martha
aliases: the sister of Mary and Lazarus
cast.note: Sister of Mary and Lazarus of Bethany who serves Jesus; the same woman in Luke 10 and John.

cast.name: Lazarus the beggar
cast.note: Poor beggar in Jesus' parable of the rich man, carried to Abraham's bosom; a parable figure, not the man raised from the dead.

cast.name: Lazarus of Bethany
cast.note: Brother of Martha and Mary, raised from the tomb after four days; appears only in John.

cast.name: The nobleman in the parable of the minas
cast.note: Nobleman in Luke's parable who goes to receive a kingdom; a parable figure.

cast.name: The nobleman at Capernaum
aliases: the father of the sick son
cast.note: Royal official whose son Jesus heals from a distance in John 4.

cast.name: Joseph called Barsabbas
cast.note: Candidate put forward with Matthias to replace Judas in Acts 1; not chosen. Distinct from Justus of Corinth.

cast.name: Justus of Corinth
cast.note: Corinthian host next door to the synagogue in Acts 18; not the same as Joseph called Barsabbas.

cast.name: Annas the high priest
cast.note: Elder high priest at the trial of Peter and John in Acts 4; the one name given in these passages.

cast.name: Judas of Galilee
cast.note: Rebel leader of the census days, named in Gamaliel's speech; never on stage.

cast.name: Cornelius the centurion
aliases: Cornelius the centurion of the Italian cohort
cast.note: Roman centurion of the Italian cohort at Caesarea whose vision brings Peter to his house in Acts 10.

cast.name: Prophets and teachers of Antioch
cast.note: The collective group of Antioch leaders who set apart Barnabas and Saul in Acts 13:1-3.

cast.name: Simeon called Niger
cast.note: Antioch prophet named in Acts 13:1, called Niger.

cast.name: Lucius of Cyrene
cast.note: Antioch prophet named in Acts 13:1, from Cyrene.

cast.name: Manaen
aliases: foster brother of Herod the tetrarch
cast.note: Antioch prophet named in Acts 13:1, foster brother of Herod the tetrarch.

cast.name: Gaius of Macedonia
cast.note: Macedonian companion of Paul seized in the Ephesian theater riot, Acts 19:29; not Gaius of Derbe.

cast.name: Gaius of Derbe
cast.note: Companion of Paul from Derbe listed in Acts 20:4; not Gaius of Macedonia.

cast.name: Ephesian Jews at the synagogue
cast.note: Synagogue audience in Ephesus who ask Paul to stay (Acts 18-19), including the hardened listeners who speak evil of the Way.

cast.name: Adam
cast.note: The first man, formed from the dust of the ground and placed in Eden; father of Cain, Abel and Seth, dies at 930 years. Appears in chapters 2 to 5 (the genealogy in chapter 5 is a list only).

cast.name: Eve
cast.note: The first woman, made from Adam's rib, wife of Adam; tempted by the serpent in Eden and mother of Cain, Abel and Seth. Chapters 2 to 4.

cast.name: the serpent
cast.note: The subtle serpent of the garden who tempts the woman and is cursed by God; chapter 3 only.

cast.name: Cain
cast.note: Firstborn son of Adam and Eve, a tiller of the ground who kills his brother Abel; builds a city named for his son Enoch; chapter 4. Tubal Cain in 4:22 is a different, later descendant of Lamech.

cast.name: Abel
cast.note: Second son of Adam and Eve, a keeper of sheep, killed by his brother Cain; chapter 4.

cast.name: Seth
cast.note: Son of Adam and Eve born after Abel's death, father of Enosh; named in chapters 4 and 5.

cast.name: Enoch (son of Cain)
cast.note: Son of Cain, whose name is given to the city Cain builds; only named in chapter 4.

cast.name: Enoch (son of Jared)
cast.note: Seventh from Adam; walked with God for 300 years and was taken by God without dying; chapter 5 only.

cast.name: Lamech (son of Methuselah)
cast.note: Father of Noah, who names his son Noah in hope of comfort from the ground's curse; chapter 5. Different from Lamech son of Methuselah's descendant in chapter 4 (see lamech_of_cain).

cast.name: Lamech (descendant of Cain)
cast.note: Descendant of Cain with two wives, Adah and Zillah, who boasts of killing a man; father of Jabal, Jubal and Tubal Cain; chapter 4. Not the same as Lamech who fathered Noah in chapter 5.

cast.name: Noah
cast.note: A righteous man who builds the ship (ark) and survives the flood with his family and the animals; later plants a vineyard and is drunk; chapters 5 to 9.

cast.name: Shem
cast.note: Eldest son of Noah, who with Japheth covers their father's nakedness; ancestor of Abram's line (chapter 11); chapters 5 to 11.

cast.name: Ham
cast.note: Son of Noah and father of Canaan, who sees his father's nakedness and is cursed through Canaan; chapters 9 to 10.

cast.name: Japheth
cast.note: Son of Noah who with Shem covers their father; chapters 9 and 10.

cast.name: Nimrod
cast.note: A mighty hunter and founder of cities in Babel and Assyria, son of Cush; chapter 10 only.

cast.name: Terah
cast.note: Father of Abram, Nahor and Haran, who leaves Ur with his family for Canaan but dies in Haran; chapters 11 and 12 (early).

cast.name: Sarai
cast.note: Wife of Abram and mother of Isaac, renamed Sarah in chapter 17; appears in chapters 11 to 23.

cast.name: Lot
cast.note: Son of Haran, nephew of Abram, who settles in Sodom; he and his two daughters escape its destruction; chapters 11 to 19.

cast.name: Lot's wife
cast.note: Wife of Lot, who looks back at Sodom's destruction and becomes a pillar of salt; chapter 19.

cast.name: Lot's daughters
aliases: the firstborn and the younger daughter of Lot
cast.note: Two unnamed daughters of Lot who lie with their father and bear Moab and Ben Ammi; chapter 19. Treat as a group on stage.

cast.name: Hagar
cast.note: Egyptian servant of Sarai, mother of Ishmael by Abram; flees to the wilderness and is comforted by an angel; chapters 16 and 21.

cast.name: Ishmael
cast.note: Son of Abram and Hagar, sent away with his mother; ancestor of the Ishmaelites; chapters 16, 17, 21, 25.

cast.name: Isaac
cast.note: Son of Abraham and Sarah, born in old age; the promised heir; married to Rebekah; father of Esau and Jacob; chapters 17 to 35.

cast.name: Rebekah
cast.note: Wife of Isaac and mother of Esau and Jacob; daughter of Bethuel, sister of Laban; chapters 22 to 35.

cast.name: Abimelech (king of Gerar in Abraham's time)
cast.note: King of Gerar who takes Sarah into his household; chapters 20 and 21. The later Abimelech king of the Philistines in Isaac's time is a different individual, listed separately.

cast.name: Abimelech (Philistine king in Isaac's time)
cast.note: Philistine king of Gerar in Isaac's time who makes a covenant with Isaac; chapter 26. Different from the Abimelech of Abraham's time (chapters 20 and 21).

cast.name: Phicol
cast.note: Captain of the army of Abimelech who makes a covenant with Abraham, and later with Isaac; chapters 21 and 26.

cast.name: Eliezer of Damascus
aliases: the eldest servant of Abraham's house
cast.note: Abraham's servant who would have been his heir, and who is sent to find Isaac a wife (chapter 24, where he is unnamed). Listed here since he is named in 15:2 and the servant of chapter 24 is the same person.

cast.name: Bethuel
cast.note: Son of Nahor and Milcah, father of Rebekah and Laban; chapters 22 and 24.

cast.name: Laban
cast.note: Brother of Rebekah and father of Leah and Rachel; Jacob serves him; chapters 24, 27 to 31. Different from Laban the Syrian mentioned in 31:20 only by context, but the same individual.

cast.name: Esau
cast.note: Elder son of Isaac and Rebekah, a hunter, who sells his birthright and loses his blessing to Jacob; chapters 25 to 36.

cast.name: Jacob
cast.note: Younger son of Isaac and Rebekah, who wrestles with a man at Peniel and is renamed Israel; father of the twelve sons; chapters 25 to 50.

cast.name: Leah
cast.note: Elder daughter of Laban, first wife of Jacob, mother of Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, and others; chapters 29 to 35.

cast.name: Rachel
cast.note: Younger daughter of Laban, Jacob's beloved wife, mother of Joseph and Benjamin; chapters 29 to 35.

cast.name: Bilhah
cast.note: Servant of Rachel given to Jacob as a wife; mother of Dan and Naphtali; chapters 29, 30, 35.

cast.name: Zilpah
cast.note: Servant of Leah given to Jacob as a wife; mother of Gad and Asher; chapters 29, 30, 35.

cast.name: Reuben
cast.note: Firstborn son of Jacob and Leah; involved in the plot against Joseph and offers to save him; chapters 29, 35, 37, 42, 46, 49.

cast.name: Judah
cast.note: Son of Jacob and Leah; urges selling Joseph to the Ishmaelites; later pledges himself for Benjamin; chapters 29, 37, 38, 43, 44, 46, 49.

cast.name: Issachar
cast.note: Son of Jacob and Leah; named in the lists and in the blessing of Jacob; chapters 30, 35, 46, 49.

cast.name: Zebulun
cast.note: Son of Jacob and Leah; chapters 30, 35, 46, 49.

cast.name: Dan (son of Jacob)
cast.note: Son of Jacob and Bilhah; chapters 30, 35, 46, 49.

cast.name: Naphtali
cast.note: Son of Jacob and Bilhah; chapters 30, 35, 46, 49.

cast.name: Asher
cast.note: Son of Jacob and Zilpah; chapters 30, 35, 46, 49.

cast.name: Benjamin
cast.note: Youngest son of Jacob and Rachel, who dies in childbirth naming him; brother of Joseph; chapters 35, 42 to 46.

cast.name: Dinah
cast.note: Daughter of Jacob and Leah, defiled by Shechem and avenged by her brothers; chapter 34 (and listed in 30:21 and 46:15).

cast.name: Shechem
cast.note: Prince of Shechem son of Hamor, who defiles Dinah and asks to marry her; chapter 34.

cast.name: Hamor
cast.note: Father of Shechem and prince of the Hivites, who negotiates with Jacob's sons; chapter 34.

cast.name: Tamar
cast.note: Daughter-in-law of Judah, widow of Er and then of Onan, who tricks Judah into fathering Perez and Zerah; chapter 38.

cast.name: Judah's wife (Shua's daughter)
cast.note: Canaanite wife of Judah and mother of Er, Onan and Shelah; she dies in chapter 38 and is otherwise unnamed.

cast.name: Potiphar
cast.note: Egyptian officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard who buys Joseph and imprisons him; chapter 39.

cast.name: Potiphar's wife
cast.note: Wife of Potiphar who tries to seduce Joseph and accuses him falsely; chapter 39.

cast.name: the chief cup bearer
aliases: the butler of the king of Egypt
cast.note: Pharaoh's cup bearer imprisoned with Joseph, who forgets him and then recommends him to Pharaoh; chapters 40 and 41.

cast.name: the chief baker
cast.note: Pharaoh's baker imprisoned with the cup bearer, who is hanged; chapters 40 and 41.

cast.name: Pharaoh (in Joseph's time)
cast.note: The Pharaoh who dreams of cattle and grain, promotes Joseph, and receives Jacob's family; chapters 12 (earlier Pharaoh), 40 to 47. The Pharaoh of Abram's time in chapter 12 is a different, earlier king.

cast.name: Pharaoh (in Abram's time)
cast.note: The Pharaoh who takes Sarai into his house and is plagued; chapter 12 only. Different from the Pharaoh of Joseph's time.

cast.name: Asenath
cast.note: Daughter of Potiphera priest of On, wife of Joseph and mother of Manasseh and Ephraim; chapters 41 and 46.

cast.name: Manasseh
cast.note: Elder son of Joseph and Asenath, blessed by Jacob in chapter 48.

cast.name: Ephraim
cast.note: Younger son of Joseph and Asenath, given precedence by Jacob in chapter 48.

cast.name: Ben Ammi
cast.note: Son of Lot's younger daughter, father of the Ammonites; named only in chapter 19.

cast.name: Keturah
cast.note: Abraham's later wife who bears him six sons; chapter 25.

cast.name: Melchizedek
cast.note: King of Salem and priest of God Most High who blesses Abram with bread and wine; chapter 14.

cast.name: Amraphel
cast.note: One of the four kings who fight the kings of the Plain; chapter 14.

cast.name: Chedorlaomer
cast.note: King of Elam who leads the coalition against the cities of the plain and captures Lot; chapter 14.

cast.name: Bera
cast.note: King of Sodom who fights Chedorlaomer and offers Abram goods; chapter 14.

cast.name: the men of Sodom
cast.note: Crowd of Sodom's men who surround Lot's house and demand the visitors; chapter 19. Acts as one group.

cast.name: the two angels
aliases: the men who came to Lot
cast.note: Two angels who visit Lot in Sodom and lead him out before its destruction; chapter 19.

cast.name: the three men at Mamre
cast.note: Three travellers who visit Abraham by the oaks of Mamre and foretell Sarah's son; chapter 18.

cast.name: Ephron the Hittite
cast.note: Hittite owner of the field and cave of Machpelah sold to Abraham for a burial place; chapters 23, 25, 49, 50.

cast.name: the children of Heth
cast.note: The Hittite people among whom Abraham seeks a burial place; they speak together in chapter 23. Acts as one group.

cast.name: the Ishmaelites
cast.note: Merchants and traders who buy Joseph from his brothers and carry him to Egypt; chapter 37. Acts as one group.

cast.name: Joseph's brothers
cast.note: The ten (later eleven) sons of Jacob who sell Joseph and later come to Egypt for grain; chapters 34, 37, 42 to 50. Acts as one group when on stage.

cast.name: the angels at the ladder
cast.note: Angels seen ascending and descending the stairway in Jacob's dream at Bethel; chapter 28.

cast.name: the man at Peniel
cast.note: The man who wrestles Jacob at the ford of the Jabbok, later understood as God; chapter 32.

cast.name: Aaron
cast.note: Moses' elder brother and spokesman; becomes the first high priest and makes the golden calf.

cast.name: Pharaoh's daughter
cast.note: Finds the infant Moses in the reeds and adopts him; she is unnamed in the text.

cast.name: Zipporah
cast.note: Midianite wife of Moses, daughter of the priest Jethro (Reuel); circumcises their son at a lodging place.

cast.name: Jethro
cast.note: Priest of Midian and father-in-law of Moses; visits the camp and advises him to appoint judges.

cast.name: Joshua
cast.note: Moses' young assistant; leads the fight against Amalek and stays near the tent of meeting.

cast.name: Bezalel
cast.note: Craftsman filled with the Spirit of God who builds the tabernacle and its furnishings.

cast.name: Oholiab
cast.note: Craftsman who works with Bezalel on the tabernacle, an engraver and embroiderer.

cast.name: Shiphrah and Puah
cast.note: Two Hebrew midwives who defy Pharaoh's order to kill the baby boys; treated as a pair.

cast.name: Moses' mother
aliases: a woman of the house of Levi
cast.note: Hides the infant Moses, floats him in a basket, and is hired back to nurse him; named Jochebed only in genealogy.

cast.name: Hur
cast.note: Holds up Moses' hands with Aaron during the battle with Amalek; also named as one left in charge of disputes.

cast.name: The elders of Israel
cast.note: Israelite elders who are gathered, consulted, and go up the mountain with Moses and Aaron.

cast.name: The children of Israel
cast.note: The whole Israelite people who leave Egypt, murmur in the wilderness, and gather at Sinai; acts as one body on stage.

cast.name: The Egyptians
cast.note: Egyptian people, taskmasters, and the army that pursues Israel to the Red Sea.

cast.name: The magicians of Egypt
cast.note: Pharaoh's court magicians who imitate some of Aaron's signs before failing.

cast.name: Nadab and Abihu
cast.note: Sons of Aaron who go up the mountain with the elders; named in the priestly garments section.

cast.name: Elkanah
cast.note: Ephraimite man of Ramathaim Zophim, husband of Hannah and Peninnah, father of Samuel; goes yearly to Shiloh to sacrifice.

cast.name: Hannah
cast.note: Elkanah's wife, barren, prays at Shiloh for a son; mother of Samuel.

cast.name: Peninnah
cast.note: Elkanah's other wife, mother of children, who provokes Hannah.

cast.name: Eli
cast.note: Old priest at Shiloh, judge of Israel forty years; father of Hophni and Phinehas; raised Samuel.

cast.name: Ichabod
cast.note: Infant son of Phinehas' wife, named for the departure of glory.

cast.name: Jesse
cast.note: Father of David and eight sons, of Bethlehem.

cast.name: Goliath
cast.note: Philistine champion of Gath, slain by David with a sling.

cast.name: Abner
cast.note: Saul's cousin and army commander, son of Ner.

cast.name: Michal
cast.note: Younger daughter of Saul, wife of David; helps him escape.

cast.name: Merab
cast.note: Elder daughter of Saul, promised to David but given to Adriel.

cast.name: Ahinoam of Jezreel
cast.note: One of David's two wives, taken captive by Amalekites at Ziklag and rescued. Not Saul's wife Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz.

cast.name: Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz
cast.note: Wife of Saul, mentioned only in the genealogy-like note in chapter 14.

cast.name: Abigail
cast.note: Intelligent wife of Nabal of Carmel, later wife of David.

cast.name: Nabal
cast.note: Rich, surly man of Carmel, husband of Abigail; dies after insulting David.

cast.name: Ahimelech
cast.note: Priest at Nob who gives David holy bread and Goliath's sword; killed by Saul's order.

cast.name: Abiathar
cast.note: Son of Ahimelech who escapes the massacre at Nob and joins David with the ephod.

cast.name: Doeg
cast.note: Edomite herdsman of Saul who reports David at Nob and kills the priests.

cast.name: Achish
cast.note: Philistine king of Gath who receives David and gives him Ziklag.

cast.name: Agag
cast.note: King of Amalek spared by Saul and killed by Samuel.

cast.name: Nahash
cast.note: Ammonite king who besieges Jabesh Gilead.

cast.name: Abishai
cast.note: Nephew of David, brother of Joab, who wants to kill Saul in the camp.

cast.name: Ahimelech the Hittite
cast.note: Hittite named as one of David's companions when going to Saul's camp; distinct from the priest Ahimelech of Nob.

cast.name: Eliab
cast.note: Eldest brother of David, angry at him at the battle.

cast.name: Abinadab of Kiriath Jearim
cast.note: Householder in Kiriath Jearim whose house keeps the ark for twenty years.

cast.name: Kish
cast.note: Benjamite father of Saul, lost the donkeys.

cast.name: Palti
cast.note: Man to whom Saul gave Michal in marriage.

cast.name: Adriel
cast.note: Husband of Merab.

cast.name: Egyptian servant
cast.note: Sick Egyptian slave of an Amalekite found by David's men.

cast.name: The woman of Endor
cast.note: Medium at Endor who raises Samuel's spirit for Saul.

cast.name: Philistine army
cast.note: Philistine armies and lords acting collectively against Israel.

cast.name: the wise men
cast.note: Eastern visitors who follow a star to Bethlehem and bring gifts (2:1-12).

cast.name: an angel of the Lord
cast.note: Messenger who speaks to Joseph in dreams (1:20, 2:13, 2:19) and to the women at the tomb (28:2-7).

cast.name: Zebedee
aliases: the father of James and John
cast.note: Father of James and John, a fisherman mending nets with his sons when Jesus calls them (4:21).

cast.name: Thaddaeus
cast.note: One of the twelve apostles listed in 10:3; named only in lists.

cast.name: Herodias
cast.note: Wife of Herod's brother Philip who urges the execution of John the Baptizer.

cast.name: the daughter of Herodias
cast.note: Dances before Herod and asks for John's head on a platter (14:6-11).

cast.name: the chief priests and elders
cast.note: Jerusalem's religious leaders who plot against Jesus and bribe the guards.

cast.name: Mary, mother of James and Joses
cast.note: Woman at the crucifixion and the tomb, mother of James and Joses; distinct from Mary the mother of Jesus.

cast.name: Simon the leper
cast.note: Host at Bethany where a woman anoints Jesus (26:6).

cast.name: the woman with the alabaster jar
cast.note: Woman who anoints Jesus's head at Bethany (26:7).

cast.name: the woman with the discharge of blood
cast.note: Woman healed by touching Jesus's garment (9:20-22).

cast.name: the Canaanite woman
cast.note: Woman from Tyre and Sidon whose daughter is healed (15:22-28).

cast.name: a ruler
cast.note: Synagogue ruler whose daughter Jesus raises (9:18-25).

cast.name: the two demon-possessed men
cast.note: Two men living among the tombs in the country of the Gergesenes (8:28-34).

cast.name: the rich young man
cast.note: Man who asks what good thing to do for eternal life and goes away sad (19:16-22).

cast.name: the two blind men
cast.note: Blind men healed near Jericho or in Galilee (9:27-31, 20:30-34).

cast.name: the multitudes
cast.note: Large crowds who follow Jesus, hear him, and sometimes shout for his crucifixion.

cast.name: the mother of the sons of Zebedee
cast.note: Mother of James and John who asks for places beside Jesus (20:20).

cast.name: the two robbers
cast.note: Two men crucified beside Jesus who revile him (27:38, 44).

cast.name: Elijah
cast.note: Appears with Moses at the transfiguration; the crowd thinks Jesus calls him at the cross.

cast.name: Zacharias
cast.note: An aged priest of the division of Abijah, husband of Elizabeth, father of John the Baptist; struck mute by Gabriel in the temple (1:5-23, 1:57-67).

cast.name: Elizabeth
cast.note: Wife of Zacharias, barren but conceives John late in life; relative of Mary (1:5-57).

cast.name: Gabriel
cast.note: Archangel who announces John's birth to Zacharias and Jesus' birth to Mary (1:19, 1:26).

cast.name: Quirinius
cast.note: Governor of Syria during the first census (2:2).

cast.name: The shepherds
cast.note: Field shepherds near Bethlehem who hear the angelic announcement and visit the infant (2:8-20).

cast.name: The heavenly host
aliases: a multitude of the heavenly army
cast.note: Angels who praise God over the fields of Bethlehem (2:13-14).

cast.name: Anna
cast.note: Aged widowed prophetess of the tribe of Asher who serves in the temple and speaks of the child (2:36-38).

cast.name: Tiberius Caesar
cast.note: Roman emperor in the fifteenth year of whose reign John begins to preach (3:1).

cast.name: Annas and Caiaphas
aliases: the high priests Annas and Caiaphas
cast.note: High priests of Jerusalem during John's preaching and at Jesus' trial (3:2, 22:54).

cast.name: The centurion's servant
cast.note: Servant of the centurion, dear to him, healed at a distance (7:2-10).

cast.name: The only son of the widow of Nain
aliases: the young man who was dead
cast.note: Only son of a widow in the city of Nain, raised from his coffin (7:11-17).

cast.name: The widow of Nain
aliases: the mother of the dead young man
cast.note: Widow of Nain whose only son Jesus raises (7:11-15). Distinct from the widow in the parable (18:3) and the poor widow of the temple (21:2).

cast.name: The sinful woman
aliases: the woman in the Pharisee's house
a woman in the city who was a sinner
cast.note: Woman of the city who anoints Jesus' feet in Simon the Pharisee's house (7:36-50). Possibly the same as Mary Magdalene but the text does not say so.

cast.name: Joanna
cast.note: Wife of Chuzas, Herod's steward, who follows Jesus and witnesses the resurrection (8:3, 24:10).

cast.name: Susanna
cast.note: Woman who supports Jesus' ministry with her possessions (8:3).

cast.name: The Gerasene demoniac
aliases: the man out of the city
cast.note: Man possessed by many demons who lives among the tombs in the country of the Gadarenes, healed and clothed (8:26-39).

cast.name: The demons Legion
cast.note: Many demons within the Gerasene man, sent into a herd of pigs (8:30-33).

cast.name: Jairus
cast.note: Ruler of a synagogue whose only daughter Jesus raises (8:41-56).

cast.name: The daughter of Jairus
cast.note: Twelve-year-old daughter of Jairus, raised from death (8:42, 8:54-55).

cast.name: The woman with the flow of blood
aliases: the woman who touched his cloak
cast.note: Woman with a twelve-year bleeding who touches Jesus' cloak and is healed (8:43-48).

cast.name: The twelve apostles
cast.note: Jesus' chosen twelve, sent out to preach and heal; also the separate seventy sent out in chapter 10 (6:13-16, 9:1-6, 22:14). Individual members are named where the text does so.

cast.name: The seventy
cast.note: Seventy disciples sent two by two ahead of Jesus, who return with joy (10:1-20). Distinct from the twelve.

cast.name: The lawyer
cast.note: Lawyer who tests Jesus about eternal life and asks who his neighbor is (10:25-37).

cast.name: The Samaritan
cast.note: Traveler from Samaria who tends a wounded man (10:33-37).

cast.name: The wounded man
aliases: the man who fell among robbers
cast.note: Traveler from Jerusalem to Jericho beaten by robbers, aided by the Samaritan (10:30-36).

cast.name: The innkeeper
cast.note: Host of the inn who is paid to care for the wounded man (10:35).

cast.name: The rich man with the barns
cast.note: Man in a parable whose harvest exceeds his barns, told by God he will die that night (12:16-21).

cast.name: The Galileans killed by Pilate
aliases: the Galileans whose blood Pilate mixed with their sacrifices
cast.note: Galileans slaughtered by Pilate at their sacrifices, mentioned in conversation (13:1-3).

cast.name: The bent woman
aliases: the woman with a spirit of infirmity
cast.note: Woman bent over for eighteen years, healed on the Sabbath (13:10-17).

cast.name: The ruler of the synagogue (Sabbath)
cast.note: Synagogue ruler who objects to a Sabbath healing (13:14). Distinct from Jairus.

cast.name: The man with dropsy
aliases: a certain man who had dropsy
cast.note: Man with dropsy healed at a Sabbath meal in a Pharisee's house (14:1-4).

cast.name: The tax collectors and sinners
cast.note: Tax collectors and sinners who gather to hear Jesus and eat with him (5:29-30, 15:1-2).

cast.name: The younger son
cast.note: Younger son in the parable who leaves home, wastes his inheritance, and returns (15:11-32).

cast.name: The elder son
cast.note: Elder son in the parable who resents his brother's welcome (15:25-32).

cast.name: The father in the parable
aliases: the father of the two sons
cast.note: Father of the two sons who runs to welcome the younger back (15:11-32).

cast.name: The dishonest manager
cast.note: Steward in the parable who reduces his master's debtors' bills (16:1-8).

cast.name: The rich man in Hades
aliases: the rich man who was clothed in purple
cast.note: Rich man in the parable who dies and is tormented in Hades while Lazarus is comforted (16:19-31).

cast.name: The ten lepers
aliases: the ten men who were lepers
cast.note: Ten lepers who beg for mercy and are cleansed; only one, a Samaritan, returns (17:12-19).

cast.name: The Samaritan leper
cast.note: The one leper of the ten who returns to thank Jesus (17:15-19).

cast.name: The widow in the parable
aliases: the widow who came to the judge
cast.note: Widow who persistently seeks justice from an unjust judge (18:1-8).

cast.name: The unjust judge
cast.note: Judge who neither fears God nor respects man, in the parable of the persistent widow (18:2-6).

cast.name: The tax collector in the temple
cast.note: Tax collector who prays humbly in the temple (18:10-14).

cast.name: The Pharisee who prayed in the temple
cast.note: Pharisee in the parable who prays proudly in the temple (18:10-14). Distinct from Simon the Pharisee and the Pharisee at Zacchaeus' town.

cast.name: The rich ruler
cast.note: Wealthy ruler who asks about eternal life and is told to sell all he has (18:18-30).

cast.name: Zacchaeus
cast.note: Wealthy chief tax collector of Jericho who climbs a sycamore and hosts Jesus (19:1-10).

cast.name: The servants given minas
cast.note: Servants in the parable of the minas who each receive money from the nobleman (19:11-27).

cast.name: The owners of the colt
cast.note: Owners of the colt at Bethany who ask why it is being untied (19:33-34).

cast.name: The chief priests and scribes
cast.note: Jerusalem leaders who question Jesus' authority, plot to kill him, and hand him to Pilate (19:47, 20:1-19, 22:2-66, 23:10).

cast.name: The poor widow
aliases: the widow with two small coins
cast.note: Poor widow who gives two small coins to the temple treasury (21:1-4).

cast.name: The tenant farmers
cast.note: Tenants in the parable of the vineyard who kill the owner's son (20:9-16).

cast.name: The owner of the vineyard
cast.note: Owner in the parable who sends servants and finally his son (20:9-16).

cast.name: The servant girl
cast.note: Servant girl in the high priest's courtyard who identifies Peter (22:56-57).

cast.name: The two criminals
cast.note: Two men crucified beside Jesus, one of whom asks to be remembered (23:32-43).

cast.name: The women from Galilee
cast.note: Women who follow Jesus from Galilee, watch the crucifixion and burial, and bring spices to the tomb (8:1-3, 23:49-24:10).

cast.name: The two men in dazzling clothing
cast.note: Two figures at the empty tomb who announce the resurrection (24:4-7).

cast.name: Cleopas
aliases: one of the two on the road to Emmaus
cast.note: One of two disciples walking to Emmaus who converse with the risen Jesus (24:13-35).

cast.name: The second disciple on the road to Emmaus
cast.note: Unnamed companion of Cleopas on the road to Emmaus (24:13-35).

cast.name: The eleven
cast.note: The remaining apostles gathered in Jerusalem after the resurrection (24:9, 24:33-49).

cast.name: John the beloved disciple
cast.note: Unnamed disciple in the text who leans on Jesus' chest at supper, stands at the cross, and is traditionally the author; distinct from John the Baptist.

cast.name: Nathanael
cast.note: Man from Cana, called by Philip; praised by Jesus as an Israelite without deceit; present by the sea in chapter 21.

cast.name: Nicodemus
cast.note: Pharisee and ruler who comes to Jesus by night; speaks up in the council; brings spices for the burial.

cast.name: the Samaritan woman
cast.note: Woman at Jacob's well in Sychar with five former husbands; testifies to her town.

cast.name: the sick man at Bethesda
aliases: the man who had been sick for thirty-eight years
cast.note: Paralyzed man healed at the pool of Bethesda on the Sabbath.

cast.name: the man born blind
aliases: the blind man who received sight
cast.note: Man born blind, healed with mud and spittle at the pool of Siloam; questioned by the Pharisees and cast out.

cast.name: the parents of the blind man
cast.note: Parents of the man born blind, who fear the Jews and send the questions back to their son.

cast.name: the woman taken in adultery
aliases: her who was taken in adultery
cast.note: Woman brought to Jesus in the temple by the scribes and Pharisees; not condemned.

cast.name: Annas
cast.note: Former high priest and father-in-law of Caiaphas, who first questions Jesus.

cast.name: Malchus
cast.note: Servant of the high priest whose right ear Peter cuts off in the garden.

cast.name: the chief priests and Pharisees
aliases: the officers of the chief priests
cast.note: Religious authorities who plot against Jesus, sending officers to arrest him and gathering the council.

cast.name: the crowd
cast.note: Multitude who follow Jesus, are fed by the loaves, shout for his crucifixion, and debate who he is.

cast.name: John's disciples
cast.note: Followers of John the Baptist who dispute with a Jew about purification and who speak to John about Jesus' baptizing.

cast.name: the servants at Cana
cast.note: Servants at the wedding in Cana who fill the water pots.

cast.name: the ruler of the feast
cast.note: Man in charge of the wedding feast at Cana who tastes the wine.

cast.name: the bridegroom
cast.note: Groom at the wedding in Cana, rebuked by the ruler of the feast for keeping the good wine.

cast.name: the angels
cast.note: Angels who sit in the empty tomb, and the angel who troubles the pool at Bethesda.

cast.name: the two others crucified
cast.note: The two men crucified on either side of Jesus, whose legs are broken.

cast.name: Theophilus
cast.note: Addressee of the book; named only in Acts 1:1 and not present in any scene.

cast.name: Matthias
cast.note: Chosen by lot to replace Judas (Acts 1:23-26) and counted with the eleven.

cast.name: Two men in white clothing
cast.note: Heavenly messengers who speak at the ascension (Acts 1:10-11).

cast.name: Holy Spirit
cast.note: Divine presence acting in the book, descending at Pentecost (Acts 2) and directing missionaries; appears as tongues of fire and wind.

cast.name: Crowd at Pentecost
cast.note: Diaspora Jews and proselytes gathered in Jerusalem who hear the disciples speak in their own languages (Acts 2:5-13).

cast.name: The eleven apostles
cast.note: The company of apostles acting together in Jerusalem (Acts 1-2, 4-6); they speak as a body at points.

cast.name: The assembly of disciples in Jerusalem
cast.note: The believing community in Jerusalem who pray, share goods and gather in the temple (Acts 2-5).

cast.name: The council
aliases: the senate of the children of Israel
cast.note: Jerusalem ruling council that arrests and examines the apostles (Acts 4-5, 6, 22-23).

cast.name: The lame man at the Beautiful Gate
cast.note: Beggar healed by Peter and John at the temple gate (Acts 3:2-10).

cast.name: Ananias
cast.note: Believer who lies about his land sale and dies (Acts 5:1-5); not to be confused with Ananias of Damascus or Ananias the high priest of Acts 23.

cast.name: Sapphira
cast.note: Wife of Ananias who lies with him and dies (Acts 5:1-10).

cast.name: Gamaliel
cast.note: Pharisee teacher of the law who urges the council to release the apostles (Acts 5:34); also Paul's teacher (Acts 22:3).

cast.name: Theudas
cast.note: Rebel leader mentioned in Gamaliel's speech (Acts 5:36); does not appear on stage.

cast.name: Stephen
cast.note: One of the seven chosen to serve tables (Acts 6:5), preacher and first martyr, stoned in Acts 7; distinct from no one else of that name.

cast.name: Nicolaus of Antioch
cast.note: One of the seven chosen in Acts 6:5; named only, does not act.

cast.name: Prochorus
cast.note: One of the seven chosen in Acts 6:5; named only, does not act.

cast.name: Nicanor
cast.note: One of the seven chosen in Acts 6:5; named only, does not act.

cast.name: Timon
cast.note: One of the seven chosen in Acts 6:5; named only, does not act.

cast.name: Parmenas
cast.note: One of the seven chosen in Acts 6:5; named only, does not act.

cast.name: The Libertines
aliases: Cyrenians, Alexandrians and men of Cilicia and Asia
cast.note: Diaspora synagogue members who dispute with Stephen and bring him before the council (Acts 6:9-12).

cast.name: False witnesses
cast.note: Men secretly induced to accuse Stephen (Acts 6:11-13).

cast.name: The Ethiopian eunuch
cast.note: Court official of Candace, queen of Ethiopia, reading Isaiah in his chariot and baptized by Philip (Acts 8:27-39).

cast.name: Candace
cast.note: Queen of the Ethiopians, named only as the eunuch's mistress (Acts 8:27); does not appear on stage.

cast.name: Ananias of Damascus
cast.note: Disciple at Damascus who receives Saul's sight in a vision (Acts 9:10-19); distinct from Ananias the husband of Sapphira.

cast.name: Barnabas
cast.note: Cypriot Levite who sells land (Acts 4:36), vouches for Saul, and travels with Paul on the first journey; distinct from John Mark, his cousin.

cast.name: Aeneas
cast.note: Paralyzed man at Lydda healed by Peter (Acts 9:33-34).

cast.name: Tabitha
cast.note: Disciple of Joppa known for good works, raised from death by Peter (Acts 9:36-41).

cast.name: Cornelius's servants and soldier
aliases: two household servants and a devout soldier
cast.note: Men sent by Cornelius to fetch Peter (Acts 10:7-8, 17-23).

cast.name: Rhoda
cast.note: Servant girl at Mary's house who recognizes Peter's voice (Acts 12:13-15).

cast.name: John Mark
cast.note: Companion of Barnabas and Paul who leaves them in Pamphylia (Acts 12:25, 13:5, 13:13, 15:37-39); distinct from John the apostle.

cast.name: Blastus
cast.note: Court official who mediates between Herod and the people of Tyre and Sidon (Acts 12:20); does not speak.

cast.name: People of Tyre and Sidon
cast.note: Delegation seeking peace with Herod (Acts 12:20).

cast.name: Elymas Bar-Jesus
cast.note: Jewish sorcerer in Paphos who opposes Paul and is struck blind (Acts 13:6-11).

cast.name: Sergius Paulus
cast.note: Roman proconsul of Cyprus who believes after witnessing the blinding of Elymas (Acts 13:7-12).

cast.name: Judas called Barsabbas
cast.note: Chief man among the brothers sent with Silas from Jerusalem to Antioch (Acts 15:22, 27, 32); distinct from Judas Iscariot.

cast.name: Silas
cast.note: Leading brother from Jerusalem who becomes Paul's companion on the second journey (Acts 15:22-18:5); also a prophet.

cast.name: Timothy
cast.note: Young disciple of Lystra, son of a Jewish mother and Greek father, circumcised by Paul and joins him (Acts 16:1-3, 17:14-15, 18:5, 19:22, 20:4).

cast.name: Lydia
aliases: a seller of purple from Thyatira
cast.note: Dealer in purple cloth in Philippi who hears Paul by the river and is baptized with her household (Acts 16:14-15, 40).

cast.name: Slave girl with a spirit of divination
aliases: the girl with a python spirit
cast.note: Fortune-telling slave in Philippi whose spirit Paul exorcises (Acts 16:16-18).

cast.name: Her masters
aliases: the masters of the slave girl
cast.note: Owners who profit from the slave girl and drag Paul and Silas to the magistrates (Acts 16:16-24).

cast.name: The magistrates of Philippi
cast.note: City magistrates who order Paul and Silas beaten and later release them (Acts 16:20-39).

cast.name: The Philippian jailer
cast.note: Jailer who is converted after the earthquake and washes the apostles' wounds (Acts 16:27-34).

cast.name: Jason
cast.note: Host in Thessalonica whose house is attacked by a mob and who is brought before the city rulers (Acts 17:5-9); distinct from Jason in Acts 17 only in name identity question with no other Jason.

cast.name: Thessalonian Jewish mob
cast.note: Crowd who riot against Paul and Silas in Thessalonica and follow them to Beroea (Acts 17:5-13).

cast.name: Dionysius the Areopagite
cast.note: Athenian who believes after Paul's Areopagus speech (Acts 17:34).

cast.name: Damaris
cast.note: Woman of Athens who believes after Paul's Areopagus speech (Acts 17:34).

cast.name: Epicurean and Stoic philosophers
cast.note: Philosophers and citizens of Athens who debate with Paul and hear him at the Areopagus (Acts 17:18-32).

cast.name: Aquila
cast.note: Jewish tentmaker from Pontus, expelled from Rome, who works and lodges with Paul in Corinth (Acts 18:2-3, 18-26).

cast.name: Priscilla
cast.note: Wife of Aquila, tentmaker, who with her husband instructs Apollos in Ephesus (Acts 18:2, 18, 26).

cast.name: Crispus
cast.note: Ruler of the Corinthian synagogue who believes with his household (Acts 18:8).

cast.name: Gallio
cast.note: Roman proconsul of Achaia who refuses to judge Paul's case in Corinth (Acts 18:12-17).

cast.name: Sosthenes
cast.note: Ruler of the Corinthian synagogue beaten before Gallio's seat by the Greeks (Acts 18:17); distinct from the co-author of 1 Corinthians.

cast.name: Apollos
cast.note: Eloquent Alexandrian preacher instructed by Priscilla and Aquila at Ephesus and sent to Achaia (Acts 18:24-28).

cast.name: Twelve disciples of John at Ephesus
cast.note: Disciples who know only John's baptism and receive the Spirit from Paul (Acts 19:1-7).

cast.name: Seven sons of Sceva
cast.note: Jewish exorcists who invoke Jesus and are attacked by a possessed man (Acts 19:13-16).

cast.name: Sceva
cast.note: Father of the seven exorcist sons; named only (Acts 19:14).

cast.name: The man with the evil spirit
cast.note: Man at Ephesus who overpowers the seven exorcists (Acts 19:16).

cast.name: Demetrius
cast.note: Silversmith of Ephesus who makes silver shrines of Artemis and incites the riot (Acts 19:24-27).

cast.name: Silversmiths and craftsmen of Ephesus
cast.note: Trade guild that riots in the theater crying for Artemis (Acts 19:24-34).

cast.name: Aristarchus
cast.note: Macedonian travel companion seized with Gaius in Ephesus (Acts 19:29), later with Paul to Rome (Acts 27:2).

cast.name: Alexander
cast.note: Jew pushed forward by the Jews to speak to the Ephesian crowd (Acts 19:33).

cast.name: The Ephesian crowd
cast.note: Crowd that fills the theater crying 'Great is Artemis of the Ephesians' (Acts 19:29-34).

cast.name: The town clerk
cast.note: Official who calms the Ephesian crowd and dismisses the assembly (Acts 19:35-41).

cast.name: Asiarchs
cast.note: Provincial officials, friends of Paul, who beg him not to enter the theater (Acts 19:31).

cast.name: Sopater of Beroea
cast.note: Companion of Paul traveling to Asia (Acts 20:4).

cast.name: Secundus
cast.note: Thessalonian companion of Paul listed in Acts 20:4.

cast.name: Tychicus
cast.note: Asian companion of Paul listed in Acts 20:4; named only.

cast.name: Trophimus
cast.note: Ephesian companion of Paul whom Jews wrongly think Paul brought into the temple (Acts 20:4, 21:29).

cast.name: Eutychus
cast.note: Young man who falls from a window during Paul's long speech at Troas and is restored (Acts 20:9-12).

cast.name: Elders of Ephesus
cast.note: Church elders summoned by Paul at Miletus to hear his farewell (Acts 20:17-38).

cast.name: Agabus
cast.note: Prophet who foretells Paul's arrest in Judea and binds his own hands with Paul's belt (Acts 11:27-28, 21:10-11).

cast.name: Mnason of Cyprus
cast.note: Early disciple in Jerusalem who hosts Paul's company (Acts 21:16).

cast.name: Claudius Lysias
cast.note: Roman commander in Jerusalem who arrests Paul, has him bound, and sends him to Felix (Acts 21:31-23:30).

cast.name: Paul's sister's son
cast.note: Nephew of Paul who warns him of the plot to kill him (Acts 23:16-22).

cast.name: Julius
aliases: the centurion of the Augustan band
cast.note: Centurion who escorts Paul to Rome and treats him kindly (Acts 27:1-44).

cast.name: Sailors and soldiers of the ship
aliases: the master and owner of the ship
cast.note: Crew and soldiers aboard the ship to Italy (Acts 27).

cast.name: Ananias the high priest
cast.note: High priest who orders Paul struck before the council (Acts 23:2) and comes to Caesarea with Tertullus (Acts 24:1); distinct from Ananias of Damascus and Ananias husband of Sapphira.

cast.name: Pharisees and Sadducees
cast.note: Rival parties in the council who quarrel over the resurrection (Acts 23:6-10).

cast.name: The forty men under a curse
cast.note: Jews who bind themselves under an oath to kill Paul (Acts 23:12-21).

cast.name: Felix
cast.note: Roman governor of Judea at Caesarea who keeps Paul in custody and hears him with his wife Drusilla (Acts 23:24-24:27).

cast.name: Drusilla
cast.note: Jewish wife of Felix who hears Paul about faith in Christ (Acts 24:24).

cast.name: Tertullus
cast.note: Lawyer who prosecutes Paul before Felix for the high priest (Acts 24:1-8).

cast.name: Porcius Festus
cast.note: Roman governor succeeding Felix, who hears Paul's appeal to Caesar and consults Agrippa (Acts 24:27-26:32).

cast.name: King Agrippa
cast.note: Jewish king who hears Paul's defense with his sister Bernice (Acts 25:13-26:32); distinct from Herod Agrippa I.

cast.name: Bernice
cast.note: Sister of King Agrippa who accompanies him to hear Paul (Acts 25:13, 23; 26:30).

cast.name: The natives of Malta
cast.note: Islanders who kindle a fire for the shipwrecked and watch the viper incident (Acts 28:1-6).

cast.name: Publius
aliases: the chief man of the island
cast.note: Chief man of Malta who hosts Paul for three days and whose father Paul heals (Acts 28:7-8).

cast.name: Brothers of Rome
cast.note: Believers of Puteoli and Rome who meet Paul on the road (Acts 28:14-15).

cast.name: Leaders of the Jews in Rome
cast.note: Jewish leaders in Rome who hear Paul explain himself and debate (Acts 28:17-29).

cast.name: Isaiah
cast.note: Prophet quoted by Paul and by the Ethiopian eunuch's scroll (Acts 8:28-35, 28:25); does not appear on stage.

cast.name: Peter and John
cast.note: Pair of apostles who act together in Acts 3-4 and 8; see individual entries.

cast.name: Diaspora Jews and proselytes of Antioch
cast.note: Antioch-in-Pisidia synagogue audience who follow Paul and Barnabas (Acts 13:43).

cast.name: Jews of Antioch and Iconium
aliases: the Jews from Antioch and Iconium
cast.note: Opponents who stone Paul at Lystra (Acts 14:19).

cast.name: The crowd of Lystra
cast.note: Crowd who wish to sacrifice to Barnabas and Paul as gods (Acts 14:11-18).

cast.name: The priest of Jupiter
cast.note: Priest who brings oxen and garlands to the gates of Lystra (Acts 14:13).

cast.name: The lame man at Lystra
aliases: a cripple from his mother's womb
cast.note: Crippled man healed by Paul at Lystra (Acts 14:8-10).

cast.name: Judas and Silas
cast.note: Pair sent with the letter; see individual entries.

cast.name: The apostles and elders of Jerusalem
cast.note: Jerusalem leaders who write the decree of Acts 15 and send delegates; a group that acts as one.

cast.name: Believing Pharisees
aliases: some of the sect of the Pharisees who believed
cast.note: Pharisee believers who insist on circumcision (Acts 15:5).

cast.name: Men from Judea
aliases: some men who came down from Judea
cast.note: Visitors who teach circumcision at Antioch (Acts 15:1).

cast.name: Lydia's household
cast.note: Household baptized with Lydia (Acts 16:15).

cast.name: The jailer's household
cast.note: Household baptized with the jailer (Acts 16:33).

cast.name: The Jews of Beroea
cast.note: Synagogue audience in Beroea who examine the Scriptures (Acts 17:10-12).

cast.name: Jews of Thessalonica
cast.note: Thessalonian opponents who come to Beroea to stir up the crowd (Acts 17:13).

cast.name: The Corinthian believers
cast.note: Corinthians who hear and are baptized (Acts 18:8).

cast.name: Believers who confess their deeds
cast.note: Believers who bring their magic books to burn (Acts 19:18-19).

cast.name: Practitioners of magical arts
cast.note: Ephesians who burn their books (Acts 19:19).

cast.name: Disciples at Troas
aliases: the disciples gathered to break bread
cast.note: Congregation at Troas listening to Paul's late-night teaching (Acts 20:7-12).

cast.name: The centurion and his guard
aliases: the centurion who delivered the prisoners
cast.note: Officials who deliver prisoners to Rome (Acts 28:16).

cast.name: The Augustan band
cast.note: Military unit to which Julius belongs; does not act as a group.

cast.name: The viper
cast.note: Snake that fastens on Paul's hand on Malta (Acts 28:3-5).

cast.name: The crowd who stone Stephen
cast.note: Jews who cast Stephen out of the city and stone him (Acts 7:57-60).

cast.name: The witnesses to the stoning
cast.note: Men who lay their garments at the feet of Saul (Acts 7:58).

cast.name: The seven chosen to serve tables
cast.note: Group chosen by the Twelve in Acts 6:3-6; see individuals Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, Nicolaus.

cast.name: Cyrenians and Alexandrians
cast.note: Jews from Cyrene and Alexandria in the synagogue dispute with Stephen (Acts 6:9); also in the crowd of Acts 2.

cast.name: Jews of Damascus
aliases: the Jews who lived at Damascus
cast.note: Opponents who plot to kill Saul at Damascus (Acts 9:23-25).

cast.name: The chief priests
cast.note: Authorities who give Saul letters to arrest believers (Acts 9:1-2, 14, 26:10).

cast.name: Disciples of Damascus
cast.note: Believers who lower Saul in a basket from the wall (Acts 9:25).

cast.name: The men traveling with Saul
cast.note: Companions who hear the voice but see no one on the road (Acts 9:7; 22:9; 26:14).

cast.name: People of Lydda and Sharon
cast.note: Residents who turn to the Lord after Aeneas is healed (Acts 9:35).

cast.name: The widows of Joppa
cast.note: Widows who weep and show the garments Tabitha made (Acts 9:39).

cast.name: Cornelius's relatives and near friends
cast.note: Gathering in Cornelius's house (Acts 10:24, 27).

cast.name: Circumcised believers
cast.note: Jewish believers who object to Peter's visit to the Gentiles (Acts 10:45; 11:2).

cast.name: Men of Cyprus and Cyrene in Antioch
aliases: some of them men of Cyprus and Cyrene
cast.note: Unnamed evangelists who preach to Greeks at Antioch (Acts 11:20).

cast.name: Visitors from Phoenicia and Samaria
cast.note: Travel companions who report the conversion of the Gentiles (Acts 15:3).

locations.name: Babel
locations.note: Site of the tower on the plain of Shinar in Genesis 11, also an early city of Nimrod's kingdom; Babylon is the same region in Acts.

locations.name: Haran
locations.note: City in northern Mesopotamia where Terah dies and Abram stays for a time; distinct from the wider Mesopotamia region.

locations.name: Paddan Aram
locations.note: Region of Haran where Laban lives and Jacob marries and has children; the Mesopotamia of Genesis.

locations.name: Mesopotamia and Haran (Acts)
locations.note: Places where God calls Abraham in Stephen's speech, Acts 7:2-4.

locations.name: Egypt (Genesis, Joseph and Abram)
locations.note: The land of Abram's famine visit and of Joseph's rule and the family's settlement, Genesis 12 and 37-50.

locations.name: Egypt (Exodus, bondage and plagues)
locations.note: The land of Israel's enslavement and the plagues, Exodus.

locations.name: Egypt (Matthew, refuge)
locations.note: Place of refuge for the holy family in Matthew 2.

locations.name: Egypt (Acts, Stephen and Paul)
locations.note: Land of Joseph and Moses recounted in Acts 7 and 13.

locations.name: Shechem
locations.note: City in Canaan where Jacob buys land and Dinah is defiled, Genesis 33-37.

locations.name: Shechem tomb (Acts)
locations.note: Burial place of Jacob and the fathers, Acts 7:16.

locations.name: Goshen (Genesis)
locations.note: Region of Egypt where Jacob's family settles, Genesis 45-50.

locations.name: Goshen (Exodus)
locations.note: Region of Egypt where Israel dwells apart during the plagues of flies, hail and darkness.

locations.name: Mount Sinai
locations.note: Mountain where Yahweh gives the law in Exodus, also called Horeb.

locations.name: Mount Sinai (Acts)
locations.note: Mountain where the angel speaks to Moses, Acts 7:30-38.

locations.name: The wilderness (Exodus)
locations.note: Desert between Egypt and the mountain where Israel wanders, fed with manna.

locations.name: The wilderness (Luke)
locations.note: Desert where John preaches and Jesus is tempted.

locations.name: The wilderness forty years (Acts)
locations.note: Desert of Israel's forty years in Stephen's and Paul's speeches.

locations.name: Ashdod
locations.note: Philistine city where the ark is placed in Dagon's temple, 1 Samuel 5.

locations.name: Azotus
locations.note: Town where Philip reappears in Acts 8:40; the same town as Ashdod.

locations.name: Bethlehem (Samuel)
locations.note: Home of Jesse and David where Samuel anoints David.

locations.name: Bethlehem (Matthew and Luke)
aliases: the city of David in Judea
locations.note: Town where Jesus is born, in the Gospels of Matthew and Luke.

locations.name: Jerusalem
aliases: the city of the great King
locations.note: The holy city with the temple, the main city of action across the Gospels and Acts.

locations.name: Nazareth
locations.note: Galilean town where Joseph and Mary settle and Jesus is raised.

locations.name: The Jordan
locations.note: River where John baptizes and Jesus is baptized.

locations.name: Capernaum
locations.note: Galilean town on the sea where Jesus lives and teaches and heals.

locations.name: The mountain of the sermon (Matthew)
locations.note: Hillside where the sermon on the mount is preached, Matthew 5-7.

locations.name: The mountain of transfiguration (Luke)
locations.note: Mountain where Jesus is transfigured with Moses and Elijah, Luke 9.

locations.name: The temple in Jerusalem
locations.note: The temple in Jerusalem where Jesus teaches, cleanses, and is presented; the Acts temple courts are the same building.

locations.name: Solomon's porch
aliases: the porch that is called Solomon's
locations.note: Colonnade of the temple where the crowd gathers around Peter, Acts 3 and 5.

locations.name: The Mount of Olives
locations.note: Hill east of Jerusalem where Jesus teaches and prays, and from which he ascends in Acts 1.

locations.name: The Praetorium
locations.note: Roman governor's headquarters where Pilate tries and mocks Jesus.

locations.name: Golgotha
locations.note: Hill outside Jerusalem where Jesus is crucified.

locations.name: Joseph's tomb
aliases: a new tomb cut in the rock
locations.note: Rock-cut tomb of Joseph of Arimathaea where Jesus is laid and later found empty; the same tomb in both Matthew and Luke.

locations.name: Bethany (near Jerusalem)
aliases: the house of Simon the leper
the village of Mary and Martha
locations.note: Village near Jerusalem home of Lazarus, Mary and Martha, where Jesus is anointed and ascends; one village across all three Gospels.

locations.name: Jericho
locations.note: City on the road from Jerusalem where blind men are healed and Zacchaeus lives; a single city across the Gospels.

locations.name: Galilee (northern region and sea)
locations.note: Northern region where Jesus grows up and ministers; in John it includes the Sea of Galilee, the same region as in the other Gospels and Acts.

locations.name: Judea (southern region)
locations.note: Southern region including Jerusalem; the same region in Luke and Acts.

locations.name: Samaria (region)
locations.note: Region of the Samaritans, where Jesus meets a villager and lepers and where Philip preaches in Acts; the same region across Luke and Acts.

locations.name: Sychar in Samaria
locations.note: Samaritan town by Jacob's well where Jesus meets the woman at the well; a specific town in John, distinct from the region of Samaria.

locations.name: Eden
locations.note: The garden planted by God in the east, watered by four rivers, where Adam and Eve live; chapters 2 and 3.; garden of God; the tree of life and of knowledge grow in its middle.; chapters 2 to 3.

locations.name: Nod
locations.note: The land east of Eden where Cain goes after killing Abel and where he builds a city; chapter 4.; chapter 4.

locations.name: the mountains of Ararat
locations.note: The mountains where Noah's ship rests after the flood; chapter 8.; chapter 8.

locations.name: Ur of the Chaldees
locations.note: City in Mesopotamia from which Terah leaves with Abram; chapters 11 and 15.; chapters 11, 15.

locations.name: the land of Canaan
locations.note: The land God promises to Abram's offspring, where the patriarchs live; chapters 12 to 50.; chapters 12 to 50.

locations.name: Bethel
locations.note: A place between Bethel and Ai where Abram builds an altar, and where Jacob sees the ladder and names the place Bethel; chapters 12, 13, 28, 31, 35.; chapters 12, 28, 35.

locations.name: Sodom
locations.note: Wicked city of the plain where Lot lives and which God destroys with Gomorrah; chapters 13, 14, 18, 19.; chapters 13, 18, 19.

locations.name: Gomorrah
locations.note: City of the plain destroyed with Sodom; chapters 13, 14, 18, 19.; chapters 13, 18, 19.

locations.name: the plain of the Jordan
locations.note: The well-watered plain where Lot chooses to live; chapter 13.; chapter 13.

locations.name: Hebron
locations.note: Place where Abram settles by the oaks of Mamre and where Sarah dies and is buried in the cave of Machpelah; chapters 13, 14, 18, 23, 35, 37.; chapters 13, 18, 23, 35, 37, 49, 50.

locations.name: Gerar
locations.note: Philistine town where Abraham and Isaac live as foreigners and where Abimelech rules; chapters 20 and 26.; chapters 20, 26.

locations.name: Beersheba
locations.note: A well and place where Abraham and Abimelech make a covenant and where Isaac builds an altar; chapters 21, 22, 26, 28, 46.; chapters 21, 22, 26, 28, 46.

locations.name: the land of Moriah
locations.note: Place where Abraham takes Isaac for the sacrifice; chapter 22.; chapter 22.

locations.name: Beer Lahai Roi
locations.note: The well where Hagar is comforted and where Isaac later lives; chapters 16, 24, 25.; chapters 16, 24, 25.

locations.name: the ford of the Jabbok
locations.note: Place on the river where Jacob wrestles with the man and is renamed Israel; chapters 32, 33.; chapter 32.

locations.name: Succoth
locations.note: Place where Jacob builds a house and shelters for his livestock; chapter 33.; chapter 33.

locations.name: Dothan
locations.note: Place where Joseph's brothers find him and sell him; chapter 37.; chapter 37.

locations.name: Dan
locations.note: A place to which Abram pursues the kings of the east; chapter 14. The later tribe is named in chapter 49.; chapter 14.

locations.name: the pit in the wilderness
locations.note: The empty pit into which Joseph's brothers throw him; chapter 37.; chapter 37.

locations.name: the threshing floor of Atad
locations.note: Place beyond the Jordan where the funeral procession of Jacob mourns; chapter 50.; chapter 50.

locations.name: the cave of Machpelah
locations.note: The cave in the field of Machpelah before Mamre bought by Abraham as a burial place; chapters 23, 25, 49, 50.; chapters 23, 25, 49, 50.

locations.name: the prison
aliases: the place where the king's prisoners were bound
locations.note: The Egyptian prison where Joseph is kept with Pharaoh's prisoners; chapters 39 to 41.; chapters 39 to 41.

locations.name: Pharaoh's house
locations.note: The royal house in Egypt where Joseph serves; chapters 12, 41, 45, 47.; chapters 12, 41, 45, 47.

locations.name: The river (Nile)
locations.note: The river where the infant Moses is set adrift and where the first plague turns the water to blood.

locations.name: Midian
locations.note: Land where Moses flees, tends Jethro's flock, and receives his call at the mountain of God.

locations.name: The Red Sea
locations.note: The sea that is divided so Israel crosses on dry ground and the Egyptian army drowns.

locations.name: Marah and Elim
locations.note: Stopping places on the desert route, where the water of Marah is made sweet and Elim has springs and palms.

locations.name: Rephidim
locations.note: Camp where Israel lacks water, Moses strikes the rock, and Amalek is defeated.

locations.name: The camp
locations.note: The Israelite encampment in the wilderness, where the golden calf is made and the tent of meeting stands outside.

locations.name: The tabernacle
locations.note: The portable sanctuary built according to the pattern shown on the mountain.

locations.name: Ramah
locations.note: Home of Elkanah and Samuel and of Samuel's burial; Samuel's house is here.Naioth in Ramah is a dwelling for prophets.

locations.name: Shiloh
locations.note: Sanctuary where the ark and the house of Eli are, and where Samuel grows up.

locations.name: Ebenezer
locations.note: Site of Israel's defeat and the stone Samuel sets up later between Mizpah and Shen.

locations.name: Aphek
locations.note: Encampment of the Philistines where Israel is defeated by them.

locations.name: Gath
locations.note: Philistine city of Goliath and Achish; also a place the ark is moved to.

locations.name: Ekron
locations.note: Philistine city to which the ark is moved and where the ark is returned from.

locations.name: Beth Shemesh
locations.note: Israelite town where the ark returns on the cart; people are struck for looking inside.

locations.name: Kiriath Jearim
locations.note: Town where the ark is kept in Abinadab's house on the hill for twenty years.

locations.name: Mizpah
locations.note: Gathering place where Samuel judges Israel and prays; also where the Philistines are routed.

locations.name: Gibeah
locations.note: Saul's home town in Benjamin where he dwells and holds court under the tamarisk.

locations.name: Gilgal
locations.note: Place where Saul is confirmed as king and where he offers sacrifice and is rebuked by Samuel.

locations.name: Jabesh Gilead
locations.note: Besieged by Nahash; later place where Saul's body is buried.

locations.name: Michmash
locations.note: Site of the Philistine camp and the pass where Jonathan attacks.

locations.name: Geba
locations.note: Place of a Philistine garrison struck by Jonathan.

locations.name: Valley of Elah
locations.note: Valley where David fights Goliath.

locations.name: Nob
locations.note: City of priests where Ahimelech gives David bread and Doeg kills the priests.

locations.name: Gath of Achish
locations.note: Achish's court city where David stays as a vassal.Also Gath as a Philistine city.

locations.name: Adullam's cave
locations.note: Cave where David gathers men in distress.

locations.name: Mizpeh of Moab
locations.note: Place in Moab where David leaves his parents with the king of Moab.

locations.name: Forest of Hereth
locations.note: Woodland in Judah where David hides.

locations.name: Keilah
locations.note: Judean town besieged by Philistines and saved by David.

locations.name: Ziph
locations.note: Wilderness where David hides and Ziphites betray him.

locations.name: Maon
locations.note: Wilderness and town near Carmel where Nabal lives and David pursues Saul.

locations.name: Carmel
locations.note: Town where Nabal's sheep are shorn and where Abigail meets David.

locations.name: En Gedi
locations.note: Desert oasis where David spares Saul in a cave.

locations.name: Ziklag
locations.note: Town given to David by Achish, sacked and burned by Amalekites.

locations.name: Endor
locations.note: Town where the woman with the familiar spirit lives.

locations.name: Mount Gilboa
locations.note: Mountain where the Israelite army falls and Saul and his sons die.

locations.name: Beth Shan
locations.note: City where the Philistines fasten Saul's body on the wall.

locations.name: Tamarisk under Jabesh
locations.note: Place where Saul and his sons are buried.

locations.name: Shunem
locations.note: Philistine encampment before the battle of Gilboa.

locations.name: Jezreel
locations.note: Place near the spring where Israel camps before Gilboa.

locations.name: the wilderness of Judea
locations.note: Desert where John preaches and Jesus is tempted.

locations.name: an exceedingly high mountain
locations.note: Place where the devil shows Jesus all the kingdoms of the world.

locations.name: the sea of Galilee
locations.note: Lake where the fishermen work, the storm occurs, and Jesus walks on the water.

locations.name: the country of the Gergesenes
locations.note: Region across the sea where the demon-possessed men are healed and the pigs drown.

locations.name: Gethsemane
locations.note: Garden on the Mount of Olives where Jesus prays and is arrested.

locations.name: the court of the high priest
aliases: the palace of the high priest
locations.note: Where Jesus is interrogated and Peter denies him.

locations.name: Caesarea Philippi
locations.note: Region where Peter confesses Jesus as Christ.

locations.name: Tyre and Sidon
aliases: the region of Tyre and Sidon
locations.note: Gentile region where the Canaanite woman comes from.

locations.name: the tomb
locations.note: Where the women and the guards encounter the angel.

locations.name: The hill country
aliases: a city of Judah in the hill country
locations.note: Hill country where Mary visits Elizabeth's household (1:39-40).

locations.name: The lake
locations.note: Freshwater lake of Galilee where fishing boats sail and storms arise (5:1-11, 8:22-25).

locations.name: Simon's house
locations.note: House in Capernaum where Peter's mother-in-law is healed (4:38-39).

locations.name: The country of the Gadarenes
aliases: the other side of the lake
locations.note: Gentile region across the lake where the Gerasene demoniac is healed (8:26-39).

locations.name: Nain
locations.note: Town where Jesus raises the widow's son at the city gate (7:11-17).

locations.name: The house of Martha
locations.note: House in a village where Martha receives Jesus (10:38-42). Probably at Bethany, though the text names only the village.

locations.name: The place of prayer on the mount
locations.note: Olive grove on the Mount of Olives where Jesus prays before arrest; named by the text only as 'the place' (22:39-46).

locations.name: The high priest's house
aliases: the courtyard of the high priest
locations.note: House and courtyard of the high priest where Jesus is held, Peter denies him, and the council meets (22:54-71).

locations.name: Pilate's hall
locations.note: Roman governor's court where Jesus is tried before Pilate and Herod (23:1-25).

locations.name: Emmaus
locations.note: Village about sixty stadia from Jerusalem where the risen Jesus shares a meal with two disciples (24:13-35).

locations.name: The sycamore tree
locations.note: Sycamore tree in Jericho which Zacchaeus climbs to see Jesus (19:4).

locations.name: The tax office
locations.note: Tax booth where Levi sits when Jesus calls him (5:27).

locations.name: The synagogues
locations.note: Places of worship in Galilee and Judea where Jesus teaches and heals (4:15-16, 4:31-37, 6:6, 13:10-17).

locations.name: A far country
locations.note: Distant land where the prodigal son wastes his inheritance (15:13).

locations.name: The house of the parable
aliases: the master of the house's house
locations.note: Houses in various parables (the rich man's barns, the wedding feast, the narrow door); not a fixed setting.

locations.name: Cana of Galilee
locations.note: Village where Jesus turns water into wine at a wedding; Nathanael's home.

locations.name: Bethany beyond the Jordan
locations.note: Place across the Jordan where John baptizes and Jesus later withdraws.

locations.name: the pool of Bethesda
locations.note: Pool with five porches in Jerusalem where the paralyzed man is healed.

locations.name: the pool of Siloam
locations.note: Pool where the blind man washes and receives his sight.

locations.name: the garden across the Kidron
locations.note: Garden across the brook Kidron where Jesus is arrested.

locations.name: the garden tomb
locations.note: New rock tomb in a garden near Golgotha where Jesus is laid and later found empty.

locations.name: Ephraim
locations.note: Town in the country near the wilderness where Jesus stays before the last Passover.

locations.name: the shore of the sea of Tiberias
locations.note: Lakeshore where the risen Jesus cooks breakfast for the seven disciples.

locations.name: Enon near Salim
locations.note: Place with much water where John baptizes.

locations.name: Upper room in Jerusalem
aliases: the upper room where they were staying
locations.note: Room where the eleven and the women gather to pray (Acts 1:13), and where the Spirit comes at Pentecost (Acts 2:1-2).

locations.name: The Beautiful Gate
locations.note: Gate of the temple where the lame man is laid (Acts 3:2, 10).

locations.name: Akeldama, the field of blood
aliases: the field bought with the reward of wickedness
locations.note: Field Judas acquired (Acts 1:18-19); referred to in speech, not shown as a setting.

locations.name: Damascus
locations.note: City where Saul is converted, blinded and baptized; later where he preaches and escapes (Acts 9, 22, 26).

locations.name: Straight Street in Damascus
aliases: the street which is called Straight
locations.note: Street where Saul lodges and Ananias finds him (Acts 9:11).

locations.name: Joppa
locations.note: Port town where Tabitha dies and is raised; where Peter stays with Simon the tanner and receives his vision (Acts 9:36-10:23).

locations.name: Caesarea
locations.note: Roman port and administrative seat; home of Cornelius, Philip, Herod's palace where Paul is held (Acts 8:40, 10, 12:19, 21:8, 23-26).

locations.name: Lydda
locations.note: Town where Peter heals Aeneas (Acts 9:32-35).

locations.name: Cornelius's house
locations.note: House in Caesarea where Peter preaches and the Spirit falls on the Gentiles (Acts 10:24-48).

locations.name: Simon the tanner's house by the sea
locations.note: House by the seaside in Joppa where Peter lodges and goes up to the roof to pray (Acts 9:43, 10:6-9).

locations.name: The housetop in Joppa
locations.note: Roof where Peter sees the vision of the sheet (Acts 10:9-16).

locations.name: Antioch in Syria
locations.note: Church in Syria where believers are first called Christians, where Paul and Barnabas are set apart (Acts 11:19-30, 13:1-3, 14:26-28, 15:30-35).

locations.name: Islands of the Aegean (Chios, Samos, Cos, Rhodes)
locations.note: Ports on Paul's return voyage (Acts 20:15, 21:1).

locations.name: Herod's palace in Caesarea
locations.note: Palace where Felix and Festus hold Paul in custody and Agrippa hears him (Acts 23:35, 25:23).

locations.name: The prison in Jerusalem
locations.note: Prison where Peter is held and freed by an angel (Acts 12:4-11).

locations.name: The iron gate to the city
aliases: the iron gate that leads into the city
locations.note: Gate that opens by itself for Peter's escape (Acts 12:10).

locations.name: House of Mary the mother of John Mark
locations.note: Jerusalem house where believers gather to pray; Peter knocks at the gate (Acts 12:12-17).

locations.name: The council chamber in Jerusalem
locations.note: Meeting place of the Sanhedrin where Peter and John, Stephen and Paul are judged (Acts 4:15, 5:27, 6:12, 22:30, 23:1).

locations.name: Synagogue of the Libertines
locations.note: Synagogue in Jerusalem where Stephen debates the diaspora Jews (Acts 6:9).

locations.name: The road from Jerusalem to Gaza
aliases: the way that goes down to Gaza
locations.note: Wilderness road where Philip meets the Ethiopian eunuch (Acts 8:26-39).

locations.name: The eunuch's chariot
